solution:
The repeated tosses of a coin are Bernoulli trials. Let \(X\) denote the number of heads in an experiment of 10 trials.
Clearly, \(X \sim B(n, p)\) with \(n = 10\) and \(p = \dfrac{1}{2}\), \(q = 1 - p = 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\) \(\therefore q = \dfrac{1}{2}\)
\(P(X = x) = {}^{n}C_{x}\, p^{x} \times q^{n-x}\)
\(= {}^{10}C_{x}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{n-x}\)

(i) Exactly six successes means \(x = 6\)
\(P(X = 6) = {}^{10}C_{6}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{6} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10-6} = \dfrac{10!}{6!\,(10-6)!} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{6} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{4} = \dfrac{10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10}\)
\(= \dfrac{105}{512}\)

(ii) At least six successes means \(x \geq 6\)
\(P(X \geq 6) = \left[P(X = 6) + P(X = 7) + P(X = 8) + P(X = 9) + P(X = 10)\right]\)
\(= {}^{10}C_{6}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{6} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{4} + {}^{10}C_{7}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{7} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3} + {}^{10}C_{8}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{8} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{2} + {}^{10}C_{9}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{9} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{1} + {}^{10}C_{10}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{0}\)
\(= \dfrac{10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10} + \dfrac{10 \times 9 \times 8}{3 \times 2 \times 1} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10} + \dfrac{10 \times 9}{2 \times 1} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10} + 10\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10} + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10}\)
\(= \left(210 + 120 + 45 + 10 + 1\right) \times \dfrac{1}{1024}\)
\(= \dfrac{386}{1024} = \dfrac{193}{512}\)

(iii) At most six successes means \(x \leq 6\)
\(P(X \leq 6) = 1 - P(X > 6)\)
\(= 1 - \left[P(X = 7) + P(X = 8) + P(X = 9) + P(X = 10)\right]\)
\(= 1 - \left[{}^{10}C_{7}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{7} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3} + {}^{10}C_{8}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{8} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{2} + {}^{10}C_{9}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{9} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{1} + {}^{10}C_{10}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{0}\right]\)
\(= 1 - \left[\dfrac{10 \times 9 \times 8}{3 \times 2 \times 1} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10} + \dfrac{10 \times 9}{2 \times 1} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10} + 10\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10} + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10}\right]\)
\(= 1 - \left[\left(120 + 45 + 10 + 1\right) \times \dfrac{1}{1024}\right] = 1 - \dfrac{176}{1024} = 1 - \dfrac{88}{512} = \dfrac{512 - 88}{512} = \dfrac{424}{512} = \dfrac{53}{64}\)
note: Removed an unmatched bracket, and the 10C10 term is added, not multiplied: 1 - [120 + 45 + 10 + 1](1/2)^10 = 53/64.

solution:
Tossing a fair coin repeatedly gives independent trials, each with the same two outcomes, so these are Bernoulli trials.

Let \(X\) denote the number of heads in 5 tosses. Then \(X \sim B(n, p)\) with

\(n = 5\), \(p = P(\text{head}) = \dfrac{1}{2}\), \(q = 1 - p = \dfrac{1}{2}\)

The p.m.f. is

\(P(X = x) = \binom{n}{x}p^{x}q^{n-x} = \binom{5}{x}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{5-x} = \dfrac{\binom{5}{x}}{2^{5}}\)

"Exactly three times head" means \(x = 3\):

\(P(X = 3) = \dfrac{\binom{5}{3}}{32} = \dfrac{10}{32} = \dfrac{5}{16}\)

using \(\binom{5}{3} = \binom{5}{2} = \dfrac{5 \times 4}{2 \times 1} = 10\).

\(\therefore\) the required probability is \(\dfrac{5}{16} = 0.3125\).
note: The fraction shown is 5C2, which equals 5C3; the line now says so.
